name: How to Move Through a Full Home Expansion from Survey to Framing

step.name: Step 1: Complete the site survey and verify zoning limits
step.text: Order an updated property survey to map out your exact property boundaries, building setbacks, and current lot coverage percentages. This confirms your proposed square footage fits within your municipality's residential development rules before you spend money on custom design.

step.name: Step 2: Create comprehensive architectural and structural blueprints
step.text: Hire a qualified drafting professional or contractor to produce detailed blueprints that specify foundation depths, wall framing sizes, roof tie-in details, and window schedules. Having thorough construction documents ensures accurate subcontract pricing and smooth municipal reviews.

step.name: Step 3: Submit permit applications and clear technical plan reviews
step.text: Provide your building plans, site survey, and energy calculations to the local building department for review. Expect examiners to verify zoning compliance, storm drainage, and structural tie-ins, and prepare to submit any requested plan corrections promptly.

step.name: Step 4: Excavate the site and pour the concrete foundation
step.text: Clear the building footprint, trench for footers, install required underground plumbing or moisture barriers, and pour the concrete foundation slab. Ensure the concrete cures properly and passes its initial municipal inspection before framing lumber arrives on your property.

step.name: Step 5: Frame the structural envelope and dry in the roof
step.text: Erect exterior load-bearing walls, install ceiling joists or roof trusses, and secure exterior wall sheathing. Once the roof decking is installed and sealed with weather barrier underlayment, the addition is dried in and protected against sudden rain.

step.name: Step 6: Run rough mechanicals and pass pre-drywall inspections
step.text: Route electrical wiring, HVAC ducting, and rough plumbing through open wall studs before adding insulation and drywall. Schedule county or municipal trade inspectors to review the rough mechanical work and framing connections before closing up the walls.
